note_on_fail_verdicts: The 2 FAIL verdicts (a_bpp_rgba32float_32, a_bpp_rgba32float_32x64) are a genuine, reproduced minimum-aux-allocation-floor finding at bpp16 (RESULTS.md §2.4), not harness defects -- run.py's verdict logic is intentionally strict-formula so the mismatch surfaces as data, not silently passes.
note_on_na_verdicts: The 2 N/A verdicts (e_storage_memoryless_read, e_storage_memoryless_read_rt) are method-limitation results: a standalone compute-kernel bind cannot read a MTLStorageModeMemoryless resource, so this experiment cannot observe memoryless compression eligibility (RESULTS.md §1).
headline_findings: Escape clause ANSWERED YES: ShaderWrite, PixelFormatView (independently, new finding), or a buffer-backed/linear layout each unconditionally disable compression -- a first driver can ship fully correct with compression disabled at zero special-case cost (RESULTS.md §5).
PixelFormatView alone (without ShaderWrite) disables compression -- resolves an ambiguity in docs/descriptors/README.md's existing wording.
MSAA auxiliary ratio pinned exactly: aux_bytes = W*H*N/32 (previously unresolved per docs/tiling/README.md §4.5).
Minimum aux-allocation floor (~128B) discovered at bpp16 when the numTexels/32 formula predicts less.

State-byte alphabet is NOT format-invariant: gradient/noise codes differ between rgba8unorm and r32uint despite identical bpp/geometry (H-S4 refuted) -- refines EXP-0017's single-format 0x03/0x15/0x7f result.

A single-texel outlier in an otherwise-uniform block produces a 4th+ distinct state, sensitive to delta magnitude and block position -- confirms a partial/defect-tolerant compression mode exists, without decoding its bit-level meaning (clean-room boundary).

replaceRegion: (public CPU-write API) correctly re-derives aux state after touching compressed content -- no manual aux invalidation needed by a driver; getBytes: transparently decompresses for CPU reads; blit copies preserve eligibility; MTLStoreActionDontCare does not crash a compressed render target.
